fields.ownerEngagementNarrative: We align rhythm to asset type: Riviera leisure owners get high-season flashes and channel mix commentary; Mérida corporate owners get negotiated-account pace and weekday ADR discipline. Investors see one KPI tree that reconciles STR to internal QA—no parallel stories. Lenders receive covenant-ready packs when debt is in play. We are transparent about sargassum, fuel, and ferry risk because owners make better decisions when the downside is named. Brand partners get QA calendars that include beach safety and energy—because guest trust is part of brand equity.

fields.outcome: We rebuilt shoulder-season pricing with minimum LOS and packaging that matched actual staffing—no rate dumps that operations could not deliver—and flexed labor to a 22% reduction in paid hours per occupied room on low weeks without service-score collapse. F&B was simplified to margin-positive dayparts only. Shoulder-month GOP swung from negative to a consistent 18–22% of revenue within two full low seasons (about fourteen months); peak ADR held within 4% of prior highs.

We renegotiated tour-operator allotments with release windows and deposit terms that protected BAR on retail, then rebalanced OTA versus direct with parity monitoring and a simple member-direct perk. Net ADR after channel cost rose even when gross BAR looked flat. Occupancy index versus STR competitive set improved 6 points in eight months; distribution cost as a percent of rooms revenue fell 140 bps year over year.

We layered a corporate transient strategy on top of RMS guardrails—BAR floors, length-of-stay rules, and promo approvals logged with expected GOP trade—then staffed sales to match real pipeline, not slide promises. Group and corporate pace reviews moved to weekly with finance in the room. RevPAR finished +12% year over year with GOP margin up 190 basis points in the same period; the owner cleared incentive fee in month ten versus month fourteen under the prior regime.

We reset all-inclusive and à la carte menus to margin-first recipes, retrained service for faster table turns, and aligned beach F&B hours to actual demand curves—recovering $340K annualized in F&B profit in the first full year. Rooms used dynamic BAR with comp-aware floors. ADR recovered to 103% of 2019 same-month levels four months ahead of the bank’s model; RevPAR led the owner-selected comp strip by 7–11% for five straight months post-stabilization.
